name: grep
algorithm: Walk a generated source tree in mgrep's order (each directory's entries sorted bytewise, depth first, names starting with a dot skipped), skip each file with a NUL byte in its first 1,024 bytes, and print every other file's path and its count of matching lines, for one pattern: an alternation with classes, case-folded (re), a literal (lit) or an ASCII-folded literal (ci) (README.md).

hand.c: the directory walk, on the platform API, not ISO C (Win32 FindFirstFileExW and FindNextFileW, or POSIX opendir and readdir), about 90 lines, with FIND_FIRST_EX_LARGE_FETCH, a performance flag Rust std's read_dir leaves out; a UTF-8 validator, 30 lines; a literal search (memchr and memcmp, 17 lines, as ISO C has no memmem); and a line splitter for files that are not valid UTF-8, 13 lines (line counts by the 11.34 review, awk over grep.c)

rust.name: regex
rust.inside: regex-automata 0.4.14 (unsafe code), aho-corasick 1.1.4 and memchr 2.8.0 (unsafe code and SIMD: SSE2 and AVX2 byte and substring searches, Teddy, chosen at run time), regex-syntax 0.8.10 (forbids unsafe code)

rust.name: walkdir
rust.inside: no unsafe code of its own; same-file 1.0.6 and winapi-util 0.1.11 (unsafe Win32 calls through windows-sys 0.61.2 and windows-link 0.2.1) on Windows

skip.c: no regex in C's std (the C cell is lit only)
no case-insensitive search in C's std (the C cell is lit only)

notes: The Mk side is the mgrep dogfood, unchanged (package Dogfoods/mgrep), run with -j 1 and MK_CARRIERS=1: one search task on one carrier. Its parallel form is the grep-j8 row.

The input is tools/bench gen kind tree, seed 5, bytes 100,000,000 (18,228 files in 2,399 directories; 15,201 files outside hidden names, 234 of them binary; 14,967 lines of output). The size is provisional: verify -publish-size in the coordinator's window fixes it. The tree has no .mgrepignore file and no line that is not UTF-8, so neither path of mgrep's is exercised (mgrep --stats printed nothing on standard error).
The checksum is the SHA-256 of the output with the tree's path written back as $DATA: each cell prints the same paths in the same order with the same counts.

C: a hand cell, lit only; its walk is the platform's API, not ISO C (ruling Q6 allows it). Rust: regex 1.12.3 and walkdir 2.5.0 from a cargo vendor tree in Mk-evidence (crates), by directory source replacement (D-835). Zig: lit and ci; its std has no regex.
